task: r6t2 - proposed ink-nearest audit rule (pending approval)
head: 8faf500
mode: proposal only. No file outside this JSON is changed. The rule is not written into the guide and no commit changes t53, r9t1, r5t4 or shared code.
problem: The current audit uses d<=6 on the label ANCHOR only. r5t4 Plan A satisfies d=3.76 at h=3.76 while the ink is 4.70 from its own wire and 1.54 from MCU-33; a reader assigns the text to the wrong net. The no-go in r5t4 was found by human inspection, not by the numeric rule. This proposal makes the missing ink-nearest dimension explicit and testable.
ruleText: For every visible net-name label L with an identified own wire W and foreign wires F: (1) the anchor must be strictly nearer to W than to every F; (2) the visible ink rectangle must be strictly nearer to W than to every F when the ink x-range intersects the own wire x-range; if it does not, ink is N/A and only the anchor test applies; (3) the existing anchor bound d(anchor,W)<=6 is retained. A label passes only if both applicable strict-nearer tests and the bound hold. Ties are not 'nearest': strict < is required. For automation, a hard fail needs a margin: fail only when a foreign wire is strictly more than 1.0 unit closer than W; a margin in [0,1.0] (including a tie) is review/warn, not an automatic pass and not a hard fail.

preciseDefinition.units: page units (8.25 px/unit in the r2t1 frames)
preciseDefinition.anchor: distance from the label anchor point (x,y) to the nearest point of a segment; point-to-segment, foot clamped
preciseDefinition.ink: minimum Euclidean distance from the visible ink rectangle (x1,x2,y1,y2) to the nearest point of a segment; 0 when the rectangle intersects the segment. Evaluate it only when the ink x-range intersects the own wire x-range; if the text sits beyond a wire end, ink is N/A and only the anchor test applies. Do not use the current y-only boxDist as the general definition: it is correct for the horizontal rows in r5t4 but misses vertical wires; a shared rect-to-segment routine is required.
preciseDefinition.ownWire: for a wire label, parentPrimitiveId is the wire; for a flag name, resolve the flag to its same-net wire (e.g. layout:wire:MCU_26:flags). If no single own wire can be resolved, the label is N/A, not a pass.
preciseDefinition.foreignWires: all wire segments whose net differs from the own net; exclude the own wire and same-net branches. Do not apply the c3 t in (0.05,0.95) gate to the ink-nearest test: a wire endpoint is still visually a wire; t stays a separate c3 rule.
preciseDefinition.strictness: strict < for both anchor and ink; equality is NOT nearest. The current r5t4 code uses inkOwn <= inkOther (line 107), so it would pass a tie; that is the specific line to change.
preciseDefinition.severity: PASS only if anchorOwn < anchorForeignMin AND inkOwn < inkForeignMin AND anchorOwn <= 6. HARD FAIL if (anchorForeignMin < anchorOwn - 1.0) OR (inkForeignMin < inkOwn - 1.0). WARN/REVIEW otherwise (ties and margins <=1.0). A WARN is not a pass; it requires a human decision.
preciseDefinition.marginRationale: Data-driven separation: the r5t4 moved-label true positive has margin 4.70-1.54=3.16; the clean normal labels MCU-25/27/28 have margins 10.0/4.72/5.09; the bus-adjacent normal MCU-33 has margin 1.00. A 1.0 margin keeps the clean labels passing, makes MCU-33 a warning, and still hard-fails the true r5t4 case. Use strict >1.0 for fail so MCU-33's exact 1.00 is a warning, not a hard fail.

filesToChange.why: t53's contract is five MAIN invariants (component counts/id sets, 55 wire id|net pairs, pages/MAIN uuid) and its exit 0/1/2 semantics. It has no text geometry, no ink bbox and no bridge-free pixel source; adding label attribution would turn a count gate into a different gate and make normal near-bus labels fail the MAIN invariant. If a hard gate is wanted, add a separate r6t2 geometry gate (or a new tNN) that consumes the pixel/ink input; do not overload t53.

normalLabelProbes.falsePositiveAssessment: Three ink-overlapping normal labels (MCU-25, MCU-27, MCU-28) pass cleanly with margins 10.0 / 4.72 / 5.09. MCU-33 is also normal and ink-overlapping but bus-adjacent: inkOwn 1.12 vs +3V3 0.12, margin 1.00, so strict nearest fails; the 1.0 margin makes it a warning, not a hard fail. MCU-35/36/37 are N/A because their ink does not overlap the own wire (text beyond the wire end); without that boundary a naive rectangle test would hard-fail MCU-37 (own 19.33 vs +3V3 0.48) and likely MCU-35/36, a false positive. No hard false positive among the normal labels that satisfy the boundary; the only warning is a genuine bus-adjacency ambiguity.

thresholdDiscussion.whyOneUnit: Clean normal margins are 10.0 / 4.72 / 5.09; the bus-adjacent normal probe MCU-33 is 1.00; the true positive is 3.16. 1.0 keeps the clean labels pass, keeps MCU-33 a warning, and still hard-fails the true positive. It is a warning boundary, not a license to pass: a warning is not a pass.
thresholdDiscussion.whatWouldChangeIt: If the pixel/ink boxes change by more than about 0.5 unit, or if a real label has a true margin between 1.0 and 3.16, re-derive from a larger sample. Do not hand-tune per label.
thresholdDiscussion.strictVsInclusive: Strict < is chosen. A tie is not nearest; the old <= at r5t4 line 107 must change. Exact equality at h=2.18 is a warning, not a pass.

applicabilityBoundary: Visible Key=Name labels only; ValueVisible false is N/A (not a pass).
Wire labels need a resolvable single own wire from parentPrimitiveId; flag names need the same-net flag wire; if ambiguous, N/A and human review.

Ink-nearest is evaluated only when the ink x-range intersects the own wire x-range; if the text sits beyond a wire end, ink is N/A and the anchor-only d<=6 check remains. This is required to avoid false hard fails: MCU-35/36/37 in W1 have ink x229.33-248.48 but own wire x150-210, so a naive rectangle test would see own ~19.33 and could hard-fail against a foreign bus 0.48 away.
Pin annotations (parent ending -eNN) and pin names/numbers are excluded; this rule is for net-name attribution, not black-glyph overlap. The original D2/D3 black overlap still needs criterion 1.
Foreign wires with the same net are excluded; own wire and same-net branches are not foreign.
The existing anchor d<=6 bound remains; this rule adds, and does not relax, d<=6.
A hard fail requires >1.0 margin; a tie or 0-1 margin is a warning and blocks automatic approval. A warning is not a pass.
Do not apply the rule to labels without a visible ink rectangle or without an own wire; report N/A rather than inventing a box.

The rule is a visual-association audit, not an electrical ownership change. Structural ownership remains parentPrimitiveId; a warning means the label may be misread, not that the net is electrically wrong.
